Description 
To enhance the domestic supply chain for essential grid components. 
Program Goals & 
Objectives 
This initiative will deploy a multifaceted approach to bolster domestic 
capabilities to withstand supply chain shocks, ensure a reliable energy 
infrastructure, and position the U.S. as a global leader in foundational 
grid technologies. 
Topic Areas 
 
• Topic Area 1:  Refurbishment and Reuse of Critical Grid 
Equipment will support efforts to mitigate supply chain 
constraints by identifying opportunities (at a Technology 
Readiness Level [TRL] 8 or higher) to reclaim components and 
materials from retired equipment from projects, storm damage, 
or end-of-life circumstances. 
• Topic Area 2:  Alternative Materials and Subcomponents 
will support U.S. suppliers and manufacturers in adopting 
existing (TRL 6 or higher) domestically sourced alternative 
materials and subcomponents to enhance the resilience of the 
U.S. energy grid supply chain. 
Eligible Applicants Domestic Entities: 
• Institutes of higher education; 
• For-profit entities; 
• Non-profit entities;  
• State and local government entities; and 
• Indian Tribes 
 See Section II. Eligibility for additional details.

1. Funding Details 
 
The award size will depend on the number of meritorious applications 
and the availability of appropriated funds. 
• Approximate total available funding: $20,000,000 in FY 2027, 
$20,000,000 in FY 2028, $20,000,000 in FY 2029, $20,000,000 FY 
2030, $20,000,000 in FY 2031  
• Approximate number of awards: 4–8 
• Approximate dollar amount of individual awards: $12–25 million 
• Approximate award project period:  60 months  
• Anticipated length of budget periods:  12 months  
 
2. Period of Performance 
 
We anticipate making awards with a project period of five years. 
 
Continuation funding (funding for the second and subsequent budget 
periods) is contingent on availability of funds appropriated by Congress and 
future year budget authority, progress towards meeting the objectives of the 
approved application, submission of required reports, and compliance with the 
terms and conditions of the award.
